About

Yuanfei
(Cheyenne) Hu

My path into computational neuroscience began with applied mathematics and with a simple kind of curiosity: how can local interactions produce stable memories, flexible behavior, or sudden loss of structure?

At NUS, I am extending this background through biomedical informatics, statistics, and machine learning. I hope to continue toward doctoral research in computational neuroscience or NeuroAI, with an emphasis on models that remain mechanistically interpretable and empirically testable.

Methods

How I work

I am most comfortable moving between mathematical formulation, simulation, statistical analysis, and machine-learning implementation. Across projects, I care about matched controls, locked validation, uncertainty, and making a clear distinction between what a model demonstrates and what remains speculative.

Python · MATLAB · SQL · C++ · PyTorch · JAX · TensorFlow · dynamical systems · simulation · statistical inference · reproducible workflows

Outside research

Other parts of my life

Dance and athletics have been long-standing parts of my life. I also enjoy sailing, skateboarding, travel, and photography. They matter to me independently of research, although they have inevitably shaped how I think about practice, movement, observation, and adaptation.
